paragraphs.title: Solomon’s Marriage Alliance, the High Places, and the Sacrifice at Gibeon

easy.explanation: Solomon made affinity with Pharaoh and took Pharaoh’s daughter.
easy.q: Whom did Solomon take to be his wife?

easy.explanation: Solomon went to Gibeon and offered a thousand burnt offerings there.
easy.q: Where did Solomon offer a thousand burnt offerings?

answers: Because there was no house built unto the name of the Lord
Because there was no altar at Gibeon
Because Solomon forbade sacrifices in Jerusalem
easy.explanation: The Temple had not yet been built.
easy.q: Why did the people sacrifice in high places?

medium.explanation: High places were locations where sacrifices were offered.
medium.q: What does “high places” mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: He brought her into the city of David until he had finished the building projects.
medium.q: Where did Solomon bring Pharaoh’s daughter until the building was finished?

answers: The people sacrificed in high places
The people sacrificed only in Pharaoh’s house
medium.explanation: The people sacrificed in high places because the Temple had not yet been built.
medium.q: What connection does the passage make between the unfinished Temple and the people’s worship?

answers: It was the great high place
It was the city of David
challenge.explanation: The text calls Gibeon “the great high place.”
challenge.q: What detail shows that Gibeon was an important place of sacrifice?

answers: He acted as king and led in worship
He was still unrelated to the people
challenge.explanation: Solomon is presented as king, worshipping the Lord and leading the nation.
challenge.q: What do Solomon’s actions reveal about his position?

answers: Marriage, bringing Pharaoh’s daughter to the city of David, and sacrifice at Gibeon
Sacrifice, building the Temple, and marriage
Building the wall, exile, and sacrifice
challenge.explanation: This is the order in which the events are described.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events appears in these verses?

short_answers.question: Where did Solomon bring Pharaoh’s daughter?
short_answers.explanation: He brought her there until he had finished the building projects.

short_answers.question: How many burnt offerings did Solomon offer at Gibeon?
short_answers.explanation: The verse says he offered a thousand burnt offerings.

short_answers.question: What had not yet been built?
short_answers.explanation: The people sacrificed in high places because there was no house built unto the Lord’s name.

paragraphs.title: The Dream at Gibeon and the Request for a Listening Heart

easy.explanation: The Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night.
easy.q: How did the Lord appear to Solomon at Gibeon?

easy.explanation: God said, “Ask what I shall give thee.”
easy.q: What did God invite Solomon to ask for?

easy.explanation: Solomon asked for an understanding heart to judge the people.

answers: The ability to understand and judge wisely
The ability to hear distant sounds
medium.explanation: He wanted to discern between good and bad and judge the people.
medium.q: What did Solomon mean by asking for an understanding heart?

answers: To acknowledge God’s mercy toward David
To describe the building of the wall
medium.explanation: Solomon thanked God for the great mercy shown to David.
medium.q: Why did Solomon mention David his father?

answers: As a little child who did not know how to go out or come in
medium.explanation: Solomon admitted that he did not know how to go out or come in.
medium.q: How did Solomon describe himself as a leader?

answers: A king must judge and lead the people
A king should only gather riches
A king should stay away from the people
challenge.explanation: Solomon asked for wisdom so that he could judge the people.
challenge.q: What does Solomon’s request show about his understanding of kingship?

answers: He was inexperienced and was about to lead a great people
He was required only to build a wall
challenge.explanation: He described himself as a little child and the people as a great multitude.
challenge.q: Why was Solomon’s request appropriate to his situation?

answers: A great people requires wise judgment
A great people does not need a leader
A great people requires only wealth
challenge.explanation: Solomon needed discernment to judge such a numerous people.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between “a great people” and “an understanding heart”?

short_answers.question: Where did the Lord appear to Solomon?
short_answers.answer: At Gibeon in a dream by night.
short_answers.explanation: The Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream and invited him to ask for a gift.

short_answers.question: What did Solomon say he did not know how to do?
short_answers.explanation: He used this expression to describe his inexperience as a leader.

short_answers.question: What kind of heart did Solomon request?
short_answers.explanation: He wanted to discern between good and bad and judge the people.

paragraphs.title: God’s Response and the Promise of Wisdom, Wealth, and Honor

easy.q: How did the Lord respond to Solomon’s request?

easy.explanation: God gave Solomon a wise and understanding heart.
God also gave him riches and honour.
easy.q: What else did God give Solomon, although he had not asked for it?

medium.explanation: An understanding person can perceive matters and judge wisely.
medium.q: What does “understanding” mean in “a wise and an understanding heart”?

answers: If he walked in God’s ways and kept His commandments
If he offered a thousand burnt offerings every day
medium.explanation: God connected long life with obedience to His ways and commandments.
medium.q: On what condition was Solomon promised long life?

answers: He returned to Jerusalem and offered before the ark of the covenant
medium.explanation: He came to Jerusalem, stood before the ark, offered sacrifices, and made a feast.
medium.q: What did Solomon do after he awoke from the dream?

answers: God valued Solomon’s request for wisdom above personal advantages
Solomon had asked for riches and honour
challenge.explanation: Solomon had asked for understanding rather than long life, riches, or his enemies’ lives.
challenge.q: What does God’s answer show about Solomon’s request compared with the additional gifts?

answers: It depended on faithfulness to God’s ways
It depended on the number of offerings
It depended on building the city of David
challenge.explanation: God said He would lengthen Solomon’s days if he kept His statutes and commandments.
challenge.q: Why is long life presented as conditional rather than unconditional?

answers: The dream led to worship, thanksgiving, and fellowship
The dream caused Solomon to leave the people
challenge.explanation: After the dream, Solomon worshipped before the ark and made a feast for his servants.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the dream and Solomon’s actions in Jerusalem?

short_answers.question: What pleased the Lord?
short_answers.explanation: The Lord was pleased that Solomon had asked for understanding.

short_answers.question: What two things did God give Solomon besides wisdom?
short_answers.explanation: God gave him both riches and honour, although he had not asked for them.

short_answers.question: What did Solomon offer before the ark?
short_answers.explanation: He also made a feast for all his servants.

paragraphs.title: The Two Women and the Dispute over the Child

easy.explanation: Two women came unto the king and stood before him.
easy.q: Who came before Solomon for judgment?

easy.explanation: One woman said that they dwelt in one house and had given birth there.
easy.q: Where had the two women given birth?

answers: He was taken to another house
easy.explanation: One woman’s child died in the night.
easy.q: What happened to one of the children during the night?

medium.explanation: Here “save” means except for or apart from.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “save” mean in “save we two in the house”?

medium.explanation: The second woman was delivered on the third day after the first woman.
medium.q: How many days separated the births of the two children?

answers: Each woman claimed that the living child was hers
The child was not in the house
medium.explanation: Both women made opposite claims before the king.
medium.q: Why was it difficult to decide immediately which woman was the mother of the living child?

answers: The woman said there was no stranger with them
She said many people were there
She said the children were born in another city
challenge.explanation: She stated that there was no stranger in the house, only the two women.
challenge.q: Which detail supports the claim that no witness was in the house?

answers: The identity of the living child’s mother
How many children were in the house
challenge.explanation: Each woman claimed the living child and said the dead child belonged to the other.
challenge.q: What was the central dispute between the two women?

answers: Births, a child’s death, opposing claims, and an appeal to the king
Judgment, births, a child’s death, and an appeal to the king
A child’s death, building a house, births, and judgment
challenge.explanation: That is the order of events described in the passage.
challenge.q: How did the story develop from the births to the hearing before the king?

short_answers.question: How many women came before Solomon?
short_answers.explanation: They came to the king and stood before him.

short_answers.question: How long after the first woman’s delivery did the second woman give birth?
short_answers.explanation: The second woman was delivered on the third day.

short_answers.question: What did each woman claim about the living child?
short_answers.answer: Each claimed that the living child was hers.
short_answers.explanation: Their conflicting claims brought the matter before Solomon.

paragraphs.title: Solomon’s Judgment and the Identification of the True Mother

easy.q: What did Solomon command to be brought?

answers: Give him jointly to both women
easy.explanation: He proposed giving half to one woman and half to the other.
easy.q: What did Solomon propose to do with the living child?

answers: Give the living child to the woman who wanted him spared
easy.explanation: Solomon ordered the living child to be given to the woman who asked that he not be slain.

answers: Her compassion was stirred for her son
medium.explanation: The true mother was moved with compassion and wanted the child to live.
medium.q: What does “her bowels yearned upon her son” mean?

answers: She asked that the child be given to the other woman
She agreed to divide the child
medium.explanation: The true mother was willing to surrender the child to save his life.
medium.q: Which response revealed the true mother?

answers: Because he truly wanted to kill him
Because he did not know there was a living child
medium.explanation: The proposal exposed the genuine mother through her reaction.
medium.q: Why did Solomon propose dividing the child?

answers: The true mother valued the child’s life above possessing him
The true mother asked for the sword
The true mother agreed to the division
challenge.explanation: Her willingness to give up the child showed her love and concern for his life.
challenge.q: What made Solomon’s decision a way to reveal the truth?

answers: She showed no compassion for the child
She surrendered him for the other woman’s sake
challenge.explanation: She accepted the destructive proposal instead of seeking the child’s safety.
challenge.q: What can be inferred about the woman who said, “Let it be neither mine nor thine, but divide it”?

answers: It changed from an apparent action into a test of motherhood
It changed from a sacrifice into an act already completed
It changed from a game into a marriage proposal
challenge.explanation: The sword was not used; the proposal revealed the women’s hearts.
challenge.q: How did the meaning of the sword proposal change during the judgment?

short_answers.question: What did Solomon command to be brought?
short_answers.explanation: The sword was brought before the king.

short_answers.question: What did the true mother ask Solomon to do?
short_answers.answer: Give the living child to the other woman and not slay him.
short_answers.explanation: She preferred to lose the child rather than see him killed.

short_answers.question: What did Solomon say about the woman who pleaded for the child’s life?
short_answers.explanation: Her compassion revealed her true identity.

easy.explanation: All Israel heard about the judgment.
easy.q: Who heard about the judgment Solomon had judged?

easy.explanation: They feared the king after hearing about his judgment.
They saw that the wisdom of God was in him.
easy.q: What did Israel see in Solomon?

answers: They stood in awe or reverence
They saw him from far away
medium.explanation: In this context, “feared” means they respected and stood in awe of him.
medium.q: What does “feared” mean in “they feared the king”?

answers: He discerned the truth in the judgment
medium.explanation: The judgment showed his ability to discern the truth and do judgment.
medium.q: Why did Israel recognize Solomon’s wisdom?

answers: The judgment caused the people to recognize the king’s wisdom
The judgment caused the people to leave the land
The judgment caused the people to oppose the king
medium.explanation: After hearing the judgment, the people recognized Solomon’s wisdom and stood in awe of him.
medium.q: What was the connection between hearing the judgment and fearing the king?

answers: It was understood to be the wisdom of God within him
It came only from his age
challenge.explanation: The text says that the wisdom of God was in him.
challenge.q: What does the end of the chapter indicate about the source of Solomon’s wisdom?

answers: It increased their respect and awe of him
It caused them to ignore him
challenge.explanation: The people feared the king after seeing his wisdom in judgment.
challenge.q: How did the judgment affect Solomon’s standing among the people?

answers: The understanding heart he requested was demonstrated in practical judgment
His request for wealth was shown by building a city
His request for an army was shown by a victory
challenge.explanation: The wisdom Solomon requested was displayed in his ability to judge rightly.
challenge.q: What idea connects Solomon’s request earlier in the chapter with Israel’s response at the end?

short_answers.question: Who heard about Solomon’s judgment?
short_answers.explanation: The whole nation heard about the judgment.

short_answers.question: What did the people see in Solomon?
short_answers.explanation: They saw that God’s wisdom was in him to do judgment.

short_answers.question: Why did the people fear the king?
short_answers.answer: Because they saw his God-given wisdom in judgment.
short_answers.explanation: His wise decision caused them to stand in awe of him.
